record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Given a word, can its minimal and maximal regular F-factorizations, measured by the length of the index sequence, be found in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Given a word, can its minimal and maximal regular F -factorization (in the sense of the length of the sequence of indices) be found in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and $A^*$ the free monoid of finite words over $A$. Fix an indexed family $\mathcal F=(F_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty languages over $A$ (the family $\mathcal F$ is given by some fixed finite description, e.g. each $F_i$ is recognized by a finite automaton uniformly computable from $i$).

An $\mathcal F$-factorization of a word $w\in A^*$ is a pair consisting of a factorization
$$w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$$
into nonempty factors $w_j\in A^*$ together with a sequence of indices $(i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_n)\in\mathbb N^n$ such that $w_j\in F_{i_j}$ for every $j=1,\ldots,n$. The sequence $(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$ is called the index sequence of the factorization, and its length is $n$.

An $\mathcal F$-factorization is called regular when the index sequence $(i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_n)$ is non-decreasing, i.e. $i_1\le i_2\le\cdots\le i_n$.

Given $w\in A^*$, a minimal (respectively maximal) regular $\mathcal F$-factorization of $w$ is a regular $\mathcal F$-factorization whose index-sequence length $n$ is as small (respectively as large) as possible among all regular $\mathcal F$-factorizations of $w$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a word $w\in A^*$, computes a minimal regular $\mathcal F$-factorization of $w$ and a maximal regular $\mathcal F$-factorization of $w$ in time polynomial in $|w|$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in the compilation of open problems from the WORDS conferences (1997–2017), originally raised at WORDS 1997 by Karhumäki, Plandowski, and Rytter. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent publication or preprint resolving the polynomial-time computability of the minimal and maximal regular F-factorizations, so the current status is unclear from publicly available sources.
